remaining_conditions: complete the remaining Linux/AArch64 reserve, commit, decommit, purge, protect, unmap, reuse, huge-page, hint, NUMA, and aligned-overmap substrate with fault-injection evidence beyond the selected direct/prefix/suffix cleanup-owner, reset-advice retry-snapshot, and native one-page protection-owner/retry slices

complete pinned C's normal _mi_meta_zalloc and _mi_meta_free behavior across remaining direct callers and lifecycles in src/subproc.c, src/init.c, src/theap.c, src/threadlocal.c, and src/heap.c, including the actual mi_subproc_t/theap_meta_lock metadata contract rather than the selected identity-only admission gate; either retire the selected synthetic regular-OS unmap witness or prove a source-faithful non-metadata _mi_arenas_free owner with its full memory-ID/subprocess contract; complete no-free, arena registry/subprocess, huge/remap, and every remaining source memory-ID ownership branch with retry-preserving failure behavior where source ownership remains live

complete source-shaped bitmap ownership, range, other visitor families, statistics, and concurrency behavior beyond the selected one-chunk abandoned-page reject/restore, accept, and stale-conservative-map repair differential, generic scalar clear-range visitor's field-bounded completed/stopped traversal, and rangesn wrapper's selected aligned-three completed/stopped, <=1 delegation, and above-field cap traces

complete multi-arena search, claim, release, purge scheduling, and reuse semantics with ownership checks beyond the selected default one-slice delayed-purge 64-bit bitmap-field callback grouping and frozen-Linux default-decommit-error consumption

complete source-order process, OS, options, TLS, arena, publication, and shutdown initialization semantics beyond the selected detached-metadata Theap's bounded first-head image/input-refusal boundary, identity-only admission publication, and static detached-metadata image/global-PageMap ordering

exercise all remaining allocation, commit, map, metadata, bitmap, PageMap, arena, and release failures without leaking or changing ownership beyond the selected native one-page protect/unprotect owner-and-retry boundary

prove every remaining M2 metadata and substrate path remains allocation-free or uses the reviewed recursion boundary under same-thread reentry beyond the selected prepared direct zalloc, aligned-zalloc, and rezalloc routes; cover C lock equivalence, reentrant callbacks or signals, cross-thread contention, and PageMap, arena, OS, release, and copy paths

exclusions.reason: page headers, free lists, local allocation, and regular-page state are not M2 memory-substrate closure
small and medium allocation behavior remains a later engine milestone
public libc backend selection, ABI integration, and production promotion are outside this substrate gate
the project contract supports Linux/AArch64 little-endian only

milestone.completion_rule: M2 is complete only when all eight categories are complete, every named condition is cleared, and current-commit native Linux/AArch64 evidence covers the full selected substrate and failure matrix.
nonclaims: the selected PageMap success differential compares source-relative transitions only, records header-layout and root-owner differences, and does not cover PageMap extension or release fault injection

the separate PageMap cold-init differential records the C static-empty-root/later-success behavior and the Rust absent-root/typed-poison result as an intentionally accepted bounded safety divergence; it does not claim a common cold lookup, public C ABI behavior, or full process-initialization parity

the selected aligned-overmap cleanup-owner tests prove Rust non-RAII ownership after direct or partial release failure; they do not claim C retry semantics, full aligned-allocation policy, or complete VM fault parity

the selected reset-advice regression proves only the private source snapshot/retry control flow with a deterministic advisory mock; it does not claim a live-kernel EAGAIN frequency or complete purge fault parity

the selected native protection test proves only one committed anonymous page under test-only pre-syscall Protect and Unprotect NOMEM injection: the mapping's base/length remain owned, failed protect leaves the page writable, and each disabled-plan retry succeeds. It does not observe live kernel error behavior or C diagnostics, prove protection state after failed unprotect, cover partial, empty, or aligned ranges, secure or guarded policy, allocator callers, decommit, commit, purge, PageMap, arena, metadata, bitmap, or release paths, signals, races, or C/Rust failure equivalence

the selected arena-purge regressions prove only default one-slice delayed-purge callback splitting at a source 64-bit bitmap-field boundary and frozen-Linux default-decommit-error consumption; they do not claim general visitor behavior, configurable purge policy, general purge fault parity, registry-wide collection, concurrent arena use, or arena lifecycle parity

the selected detached-metadata checks prove only that Rust binds its static detached metadata image before global PageMap publication and, for the bounded same-subprocess, empty-head, non-threadpool input, preserves kind-only static provenance and frozen normal enabled page-reclaim, initializes a possibly-weak random context, and derives an odd cookie before first session/backing. After that bounded image is fully formed, preparation one-way Release-CAS publishes its exact identity through a comparison-only Rust MainSubprocess slot; COLD direct zalloc, aligned zalloc, and rezalloc(None) refuse before the metadata lock, mapping, or capability creation. A nonempty head, mismatched subprocess, or thread-pool input is rejected before mutation rather than claiming C's locked list/split or option-adjustment path. This does not model the actual mi_subproc_t::theap_meta field/layout, theap_meta_lock, a dereference-capable subprocess API, actual main-Heap linkage, or normal C metadata backing, nor establish complete _mi_theap_init, metadata, initialization, mutable-options, or fault-injection parity

the selected same-thread metadata recursion regression proves only Rust marker rejection for prepared direct zalloc, aligned-zalloc, and rezalloc before first backing or old-capability claim, plus post-drop recovery. It is not a C nonrecursive-lock or deadlock equivalence claim and does not cover reentrant callbacks or signals, cross-thread contention or races, PageMap, arena, OS, release, copy, or general metadata lifecycle paths

the selected later-TLD direct-Malloc check proves only an isolated ticket-zero static teardown without a metadata capability, one injected post-ready direct-zeroed metadata failure that consumes its later sequence without a live capability or lease, and one retry's typed subprocess-attached/no-theap Malloc capability through exact-owner teardown. It does not establish pinned C normal _mi_meta_zalloc backing, full mi_tld_init/mi_tld_free lock/list behavior, arbitrary thread/ticket behavior, or generic _mi_meta_free branch parity

the selected nonexclusive dynamic-Theap direct-Malloc check proves only one child-thread, caller-pinned empty-Heap lifecycle after ticket zero: a sequence-one Malloc TLD and a nonexclusive Malloc Theap have the selected one-member TLD/Heap list shape. Its no-page implementation releases regular backing, then the exact Theap, then the TLD. The audit observes four attached metadata capabilities (TLD, Theap, regular backing, and the distinct registry bitmap), one registry bitmap after attachment teardown, and test-only quiescent registry shutdown returning that audit to zero. It does not establish normal C _mi_meta_zalloc backing, the exclusive-arena _mi_arenas_alloc branch, generic _mi_meta_free dispatch, arbitrary Theap/list/refcount policy, page ownership, concurrent lifecycle, or process/thread shutdown parity

the selected thread-local live-rezalloc check proves only one isolated child-thread direct-Malloc regular-backing replacement after a first 16-slot image: an injected pre-allocation failure restores the old root, count, slots, and capability, then one 16-to-32 retry copies slot 15 and publishes slot 16. It observes one live capability with high-water two before teardown and zero live afterward. It does not establish normal C _mi_meta_zalloc backing, arbitrary growth, generic _mi_meta_free dispatch, full TLS/TLD/Theap/registry lifecycle, concurrency, pthread/process lifecycle, or ABI integration

the selected bitmap differentials compare only three one-chunk source-snapshot paths: an abandoned-page claim at sequence five, where a keep-set rejection restores bit 17 and its conservative map, a later accepted claim clears the bit while retaining that map, and a drained probe repairs it without a callback; the direct generic scalar clear-range visitor, where a completed walk emits source-64-bit-field-bounded runs while retaining its conservative map and a stopped callback restores only its unvisited same-field residual; and direct rangesn wrapper calls. The rangesn trace uses fresh rngslices-three images for aligned completed windows, partial-window/top-suffix retention, and a stopped callback that restores an earlier skipped window plus later snapshot bits; it separately executes the <=1 generic delegation and caps 65 at 64. These do not establish the C keep_set=false rejection route, multi-chunk or sequence distribution, actual minimal-purge/transparent-huge-page policy, actual arena/subprocess ownership, races, clear-once-set, other visitor families, statistics, binned bitmap behavior, flexible-array allocation ownership, or allocator integration
this gate does not claim a production allocator backend or any later allocator milestone
this gate does not claim non-AArch64 support
